page: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a bare metal server in the Bare Metal NVMe family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC 4345P processor operating at 3.9 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs via two threads per core. The hardware profile includes 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and is bundled with 3890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and does not contain a GPU.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is strong, with Geekbench multi-core scoring in the top 25%, while stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores fall in the middle 50%. Memory performance shows a notable tradeoff: the Passmark memory score ranks in the top 10%, but large-block write memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

This server is suited for workloads requiring high single-core CPU throughput and substantial local storage, such as database operations, text and image processing, and lightweight LLM text generation. Its dedicated resource allocation and high local storage density relative to its 16 vCPUs provide qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy applications that do not require GPU acceleration.
description: Vultr vbm-8c-64gb-amd is a bare metal server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC 4345P x86_64 processor with 8 physical cores, 16 vCPUs, and a 3.9 GHz clock speed. Equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM and a substantial 3890 GB local NVMe SSD, this server delivers top-tier single-core CPU and memory benchmark performance, ranking in the top 10% for Geekbench single-core and Passmark memory tests. However, it exhibits a performance tradeoff with weak large-block write memory bandwidth, which falls in the bottom 25%. Multi-core processing and database operations perform in the average tier. Lacking a GPU, this configuration is optimized for storage-intensive workloads, database management, text and image processing, and single-threaded applications that benefit from dedicated hardware resources and high-capacity local NVMe storage.
